originalBehavior: The route shell wraps the experience with an Engineering Sandbox lab hero, a neutral provenance footer, and a responsive dashboard layout with a stage area, HUD grid, and control bench.
localStatus: The route uses the shared Engineering Sandbox lab variant (data-story-shell='engineering-sandbox', data-story-variant='lab', data-story-nav='none') with a night-sky theme in css/stargazing.css. The hero carries a lab contract callout, story chips, and metadata. The public footer uses neutral provenance. All assets are subpath-relative. A route-local mobile override collapses the lab hero grid to a single column at <=920px because the shared lab-variant grid rule has no mobile collapse and out-specifies the generic one.
notes: The shell provides the lab framework, hero, and provenance footer. Generated chapter navigation is disabled (data-story-nav='none').
Public provenance is neutral (referenceMode='neutral', no referenceUrl) because the route is an original local build.
css/stargazing.css loads before engineering-sandbox.css, so the route mobile override raises specificity (chained shell+variant attributes plus both grid classes) rather than relying on source order.
#shortcut-help uses hidden attribute (not display:none or visible toggle) so smoke tests detect it as 'attached' state, not 'visible'.
#shortcut-toggle toggles the help panel; #sky-tooltip performs throttled picking while the pointer moves over #sky-canvas.
Input[type=range] controls for zoom, brightness, starScale, and magLimit carry [data-display] attributes bound via hud.renderDisplay.
evidence: Body elements: data-story-shell='engineering-sandbox', data-story-variant='lab', data-story-nav='none', neutral provenance footer.
Mobile probe at 390x844: .story-hero__grid computes a single 326px column with no horizontal overflow (docScrollWidth=390, bodyScrollWidth=382).
The dashboard splits into a stage canvas area and a HUD/control grid that collapse to single column on narrow viewports.
#shortcut-help is 'attached' (not 'visible') — smoke tests and direct probe confirm it's present in the DOM with hidden attribute.
#sky-tooltip is also 'attached' state, matching the re-usable tooltip contract.
Display telemetry: [data-display-value] readouts show live zoom/FOV/opacity/star scale/magnitude limit values.

originalBehavior: Astronomy math API (window.StargazingAstro) computing Julian date, GMST/LST hours, equatorial-to-horizontal conversion, and sun/moon/planet positions using standard low-precision algorithms, with hours/degrees as the input/output contract.
localStatus: Implemented in full. julianDate converts UTC milliseconds to JD; gmstHours/lstHours apply the longitude offset; equatorialToHorizontal returns topocentric {altDeg, azDeg} via hour angle and observer latitude; sunPosition, moonPosition, and planetPosition return real equatorial coordinates. Verified by Node unit tests (node --test) and by live HUD/scene readouts.
notes: Sky mapping used downstream: x=cos(alt)sin(az), y=sin(alt), z=-cos(alt)cos(az).
Inputs/outputs use hours for sidereal time and degrees for angles, matching the frozen module contract.
evidence: window.StargazingAstro exposes julianDate, gmstHours, lstHours, equatorialToHorizontal, sunPosition, moonPosition, planetPosition.
node --test passes for the astro unit suite (part of the 22-test run).
The HUD telemetry and time panels show non-zero LST and altitude/azimuth values that change with location and time.

originalBehavior: A frozen state store on window.StargazingState exposing getState, setState, subscribe, and advanceTime, with observer, time, toggles, weather, selectedTargetId, and look fields.
localStatus: Shipped with the full API. setState shallow-merges nested keys and notifies subscribers; subscribe returns an unsubscribe function; advanceTime is a pure helper. The store now drives live rendering subscribers (scene, HUD, controls).
notes: The state shape is frozen; behavior was layered on without removing or renaming keys.
getState returns a fresh clone each call; set({ time: { playing: true } }) updates only time.playing.
state.display.{zoom, brightness, starScale, magLimit} drive scene rendering: zoom→FOV, brightness→opacity, starScale→point size, magLimit→visible magnitude filter.
evidence: window.StargazingState exposes getState, setState, subscribe, advanceTime.
node --test covers state merge and subscribe semantics.
Live interaction (time scrub, weather sliders, toggles) propagates through the store into the scene.

originalBehavior: Pointer-drag and keyboard look controls that write azimuth and altitude into the state store, with 0.15 deg/pixel drag sensitivity, 3-degree arrow-key steps, altitude clamped to [-90, 90], and a { dispose() } cleanup handle.
localStatus: Shipped in full. Pointer capture, keyboard navigation, clamp/wrap math, and listener-bag cleanup are implemented and degrade to a noop handle when canvas or state is missing.
notes: DRAG_DEGREES_PER_PIXEL=0.15 and KEY_STEP_DEGREES=3 are frozen constants.
Altitude clamps to [-90, 90]; azimuth wraps.
evidence: window.StargazingControls.createLookControls accepts canvas and state and returns { dispose }.
Dragging the canvas updates state.look azimuth/altitude; arrow keys step the look angles.
dispose() removes all event listeners.

originalBehavior: Lazy async catalog loaders (window.StargazingCatalog) for stars, constellations, and meteor showers from local JSON, each returning a Promise of parsed data, with validation helpers and a magnitude limit driven by light pollution.
localStatus: Shipped and backed by real data. loadStars resolves 2863 naked-eye stars; loadConstellations resolves 88 names and 739 line segments; loadMeteorShowers resolves authored radiants. visibleMagnitudeLimit maps light pollution 0->6.5 and 1->4.0. Verified firsthand via the QA probe.
notes: Star format: { i (catalog index), ra (right ascension in hours, 0-24), dec (declination in degrees, -90..90), mag (visual magnitude), bv (optional B-V color index), n (optional name) } from an HYG/Yale-derived subset.
Constellation format: { names: { id -> displayName }, lines: [ [starIndexA, starIndexB], ... ] } authored from IAU stick figures.
Fetch is lazy and uses relative ./data/ paths for subpath hosting.
evidence: QA probe reports 2863 stars, 88 constellation names, and 739 line segments loaded.
Lowering light pollution increases the visible star count via visibleMagnitudeLimit.
Data files exist under stargazing-dashboard/data/ and load without 404s.

originalBehavior: Three.js scene lifecycle (window.StargazingScene.createScene) accepting canvas, state, catalog, and astro adapters, returning { start, stop, resize }, and rendering a star field, constellation lines, sun/moon/planets, and a horizon against a first-person topocentric dome.
localStatus: Implemented in full against vendored Three.js r70 (UMD). createScene builds a WebGLRenderer, PerspectiveCamera, and Scene; the render loop advances state time and calls camera.lookAt. Star and constellation geometry use the r70 API (addAttribute, PointCloud/PointCloudMaterial, LinePieces, VertexColors). Two runtime defects were root-caused and fixed: a visibility bug (empty-geometry objects stayed hidden until vertex count > 0) and a drawArrays buffer-binding flood caused by reassigning geometry on a rendered object. The fix recreates point/line objects (disposeOldObject, recreatePointObject, recreateLineObject) instead of swapping geometry.
notes: Vendored Three.js r70 mandates addAttribute, PointCloud, PointCloudMaterial, LinePieces, and VertexColors; PointsMaterial, LineSegments, and setAttribute do not exist in r70.
Geometry updates RECREATE the object (new PointCloud/Line, dispose + remove old) rather than reassigning .geometry, which avoids stale GL buffer bindings under r70.
rebuildStarCloud and rebuildConstellationLines recreate their objects; maybeRefreshCatalogDerivedGeometry re-runs rebuildStarCloud when light pollution or the effective magnitude cap changes.
evidence: window.StargazingScene.createScene returns { start, stop, resize } and mounts a live WebGL canvas (non-clear pixels confirmed by probe).
drawArrays buffer-binding diagnostic: 0 failures across 3140 draws through the full interaction sequence.
Screenshots show stars, constellation lines, horizon, and HUD rendering; weather dimming is visible.
state.display.{zoom, brightness, starScale, magLimit} drive FOV, star opacity, point size, and magnitude filtering; the user limit is capped by the weather-derived naked-eye limit.
Input[type=range] elements carry [data-display] attrs for zoom, brightness, starScale, magLimit bound via hud.renderDisplay().

originalBehavior: Constellation line overlay on the sky dome that reads catalog data, draws stick figures, and toggles visibility from state.toggles.constellations.
localStatus: Implemented. Constellation line geometry is built from authored RA/Dec pairs transformed to topocentric alt-az, rendered as r70 Line objects, and shown/hidden by the constellations toggle. Recreated (not geometry-swapped) on catalog-derived refresh.
notes: 739 line segments across 88 constellations are drawn from the catalog.
Lines use the r70 LinePieces/VertexColors path; frustumCulled is disabled so dome lines are not clipped.
evidence: Toggling data-toggle='constellations' shows/hides the line overlay (verified in QA probe).
Probe reports 739 constellation line segments present in the scene.

originalBehavior: HUD adapter (window.StargazingHud.createHud) binding location, time, weather, and toggle controls to the state store and refreshing telemetry, weather, meteors, targets, time, and location panels via update().
localStatus: Implemented in full. All controls are bound (lat/lon inputs, time speed select, play/now buttons, time scrubber, weather range sliders, toggle checkboxes), and update() renders live panel content for each HUD section. DOM lookups are guarded.
notes: Weather sliders use data-weather attributes; lightpollution maps to state.weather.lightPollution (camelCase).
The time scrubber spans a 48h window: baseUtcMs + ((value - 50) / 50) * 24h.
renderDisplay reads state.display.{zoom, brightness, starScale, magLimit} and writes [data-display-value] onto sibling DOM nodes.
evidence: window.StargazingHud.createHud returns { update } and panels show live values (LST, altitude/azimuth, weather, targets).
Input[type=range] with [data-display] attrs show live value readouts via [data-display-value] in the rendered HUD.
Changing inputs/sliders/toggles fires the correct state.setState patches and updates the rendered panels.

originalBehavior: Guided target navigation that slews the camera to notable sky targets via a labeled picker, using a smooth shortest-path interpolation that can be cancelled by new input.
localStatus: Implemented. Seven guided target buttons render as a sibling picker of the HUD body; selecting one slerps the look direction along the shortest azimuth path with an ease-in-out over roughly 800ms, cancelling on a new selection or pointerdown.
notes: Slew uses shortest-azimuth easing to avoid the long way around the dome.
Active slews cancel on a new target pick or manual pointer drag.
evidence: QA probe finds 7 guided buttons and confirms a slerp animation on selection.
Screenshot after guided navigation shows the camera re-aimed at the chosen target.

originalBehavior: Weather sandbox with cloud cover, seeing, and light-pollution sliders feeding the state store to drive atmospheric effects (star dimming, twinkle, horizon brightness), with no live weather API.
localStatus: Implemented and connected to rendering. The three sliders (cloud, seeing, lightpollution) drive star dimming and the visible magnitude limit; cloud cover visibly dims the field, and light pollution reduces the visible star count. Defaults: cloud=0.18, seeing=0.74, lightPollution=0.32.
notes: Values are abstract 0-1 ranges; no external API calls are made.
Light pollution drives visibleMagnitudeLimit (0->6.5, 1->4.0); the effective limit is min(display.magLimit, visibleMagnitudeLimit), and changes rebuild the star cloud.
evidence: Three input[type=range] elements with data-weather='cloud', 'seeing', 'lightpollution'.
QA probe confirms weather dimming changes the rendered field; screenshot 03 shows the dimmed state.

originalBehavior: WebGL detection and graceful fallback: main.js tests the canvas context on load, sets body.dataset.stargazingReady to 'true' or 'fallback', and unhides #stargazing-fallback when WebGL is unavailable.
localStatus: Implemented in full. hasWebGL tries 'webgl' and 'experimental-webgl' and catches exceptions; bootstrap sets stargazingReady='true' only when scene.start() confirms renderer initialization, otherwise it shows the fallback and sets 'fallback'. Optional UI adapters remain guarded.
notes: #stargazing-fallback is always present in the DOM (hidden by default) for screen readers.
main.js loads last so all adapters are available at bootstrap.
evidence: QA probe confirms body.dataset.stargazingReady='true' in headless Chromium with no console errors or 404s.
The eight expected window.Stargazing* globals are present after load.
#tonight-button selects visible targets and opens #object-details; #details-close and Escape close it.
#shortcut-toggle toggles #shortcut-help (hidden ↔ visible); #sky-tooltip performs requestAnimationFrame-throttled canvas picking and ignores projected points outside the camera frustum.
T/L/C/R shortcut keys (telescope/light/constellations/reset) fire when not focused on an input or textarea.

originalBehavior: Route-local JSON data files for stars, constellations, and meteor showers with authored, verified content.
localStatus: Shipped. stargazing-dashboard/data/ contains stars.json (2863 entries), constellations.json (88 names / 739 lines), and meteor-showers.json. Files load via relative fetch at runtime with no 404s.
notes: Star data is an HYG/Yale-derived naked-eye subset; constellation data is authored IAU stick figures.
Files are loaded with relative ./data/ paths for subpath hosting under /interactive-explanation/.
evidence: catalog loaders resolve 2863 stars and 88/739 constellation names/lines firsthand.
smoke-bundle and the QA probe load the route with no network failures.

localStatus: Manifest synchronization owns the body Engineering Sandbox metadata and shared head seams while preserving Route runtime placement.
notes: Ticket 12 synchronizes the manifest-owned Engineering Sandbox body contract and shared head seams without moving existing Route runtimes or scripts.
evidence: Route HTML declares canonical data-story metadata plus one color-scheme meta, synchronous theme init before Route styles, Sandbox CSS after Route styles, and one deferred Sandbox runtime whose existing position is preserved.
